# 08 — UI/UX Design System

**Source of truth:** `design-system/lead-scoring-pipeline/MASTER.md`, generated by the UI/UX Pro Max skill for category **Analytics Dashboard** at dials *variance 3/10 (centred, minimal) · motion 2/10 (subtle) · density 8/10 (dense dashboard)*. This doc records how those tokens apply to this pipeline's one surface, and what the surface deliberately will not do.

When building a page: read `MASTER.md` first, then `design-system/lead-scoring-pipeline/pages/<page>.md` if one exists — the page file overrides the master.

## The honest constraint

The demo surface is **Streamlit**, chosen because P1's deliverable is the pipeline and a three-page UI in one file is the cheapest credible way to show it. Streamlit does not accept an arbitrary design system: layout is its own, components are its own, and fighting it with injected CSS produces a brittle page that breaks on upgrade.

So the design system is applied at three levels, and no further:

1. **Theme tokens** — colour, fonts, radius, via `.streamlit/config.toml`. Fully supported.
2. **Composition** — what sits where, density, hierarchy, reading order, states. Fully under our control.
3. **Chart styling** — matplotlib/Plotly figures styled from the tokens. Fully under our control.

Deliberately **not** attempted: custom component chrome, bespoke tables, animation, custom focus rings. React arrives in P3; a half-restyled Streamlit would look worse than a clean one. Recorded as OQ-5.

## Tokens in use

| Role | Hex | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | `#1E40AF` | headers, grade A chip, primary chart series, links |
| On primary | `#FFFFFF` | text on primary fills |
| Secondary | `#3B82F6` | secondary chart series, hover |
| Accent | `#D97706` | the single call-to-action per page, grade B chip |
| On accent | `#000000` | text on accent fills |
| Background | `#F8FAFC` | page |
| Foreground | `#1E3A8A` | body text |
| Card | `#FFFFFF` | panels, table surface |
| Muted | `#E9EEF6` | table zebra rows, disabled |
| Muted foreground | `#475569` | captions, units, secondary labels |
| Border | `#DBEAFE` | table and panel edges |
| Destructive | `#DC2626` | errors only — never a grade, never a data series |
| Ring | `#1E40AF` | focus |

**This palette is pinned in `.streamlit/config.toml`, not only in the stylesheet.** A light theme that leaves the text colour to Streamlit inherits it from the viewer's operating system, and on a dark-mode machine the result was near-white text on the near-white background this table specifies (D-035). The three places these values live — this table, `design-system/lead-scoring-pipeline/MASTER.md` and `.streamlit/config.toml` — change together or not at all; `tests/test_dashboard.py` checks the third against the first.

**Typography:** headings **Fira Code**, body **Fira Sans**. The monospaced heading is intentional for a data tool: it signals precision and keeps numeric column headers aligned. All numbers — scores, metrics, probabilities — render in Fira Code with tabular figures so digits line up in a dense column.

**Spacing (density 8/10):** `xs 2px · sm 4px · md 8px · lg 12px · xl 16px · 2xl 24px · 3xl 32px`. Table rows use `md`; panels use `lg`; only the page container uses `3xl`. A dense table is the point — a rep scans 200 rows, so generous padding is a cost, not a courtesy.

**Shadows:** `sm` for the table surface, `md` for panels. Nothing above `md`. No shadow on anything that is not lifted off the page.

**Motion (2/10):** a 150–200 ms opacity transition on hover and on results appearing. Nothing else. Every transition is skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Grade chips — the one piece of visual semantics

The grade is the fastest thing on the page to read, so it gets colour, and nothing else competes for it.

| Grade | Fill | Text | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | `#1E40AF` primary | `#FFFFFF` | top 20%: highest emphasis, cold-hue authority rather than "success green" — the lead is *likely*, not *won* |
| **B** | `#D97706` accent | `#000000` | next 30%: warm, clearly distinct from A at a glance |
| **C** | `#E9EEF6` muted | `#475569` | the rest: recedes, still legible; **never red** — a C lead is deprioritised, not an error |

Each chip also carries its letter, so the grade never depends on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Contrast: white on `#1E40AF` ≈ 8.6:1, black on `#D97706` ≈ 8.4:1, `#475569` on `#E9EEF6` ≈ 7.0:1 — all clear of the 4.5:1 floor.

## Page-level composition

**Rank leads** (default): one-line purpose at top → upload control → when results exist: a four-tile summary row (leads scored · grade A count · mean score · model version), then the dense table, then the download button. The table is the hero; the summary tiles exist to orient, not to decorate. Sorted by score descending. Sticky header. Horizontal scroll inside the table wrapper, never on the page (the skill's responsive rule on table overflow).

**Try one lead:** a single column of fields in the order a rep would learn them — source, then behaviour, then profile. Every field labelled in business language with its unit (`Time on website (seconds)`), prefilled with the dataset median or mode so the form is never empty. Result panel appears below the form, not in a dialog, so the inputs stay visible and a value can be changed to see the score move.

**Model card:** read-only, one column, in this order — version and training date, the results table, reliability curve, score distribution by outcome, feature importance, grade bands, then **"What this model must not be used for"**. The limits section is last because it is what a careful reader wants after the numbers, and it is never collapsed behind a toggle.

The model version is in the footer of every page, so any screenshot is attributable.

## Required states

Every state is designed, not left to the framework's default:

| State | Rank leads | Try one lead | Model card |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Empty | what to upload, the required columns, and a sample CSV to download | the prefilled form (never blank) | n/a |
| Loading | progress with the row count being scored, layout held so nothing jumps | inline spinner on the button | n/a |
| Success | table + summary tiles + download | result panel with score, grade, three reasons | the figures |
| Error — bad input | names the missing column; the file stays in session | field-level message, form state kept | n/a |
| Error — service down | "the scoring service is not responding", retry, upload preserved | same | "metrics unavailable" rather than blanks |
| Partial | over 1,000 rows: offers to score the first 1,000 and says so plainly | n/a | n/a |

No empty white space, no bare exception text, no silently truncated results.

## Charts

The skill's chart database is oriented to product analytics and does not cover ML diagnostics, so chart choice here follows standard evaluation practice, styled with the tokens above. Load the `dataviz` skill before writing the first chart.

| Figure | Form | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reliability (calibration) curve | line, predicted vs observed, with the 45° reference | reference line `#475569` dashed; model line `#1E40AF`; equal axes, both 0–1 |
| ROC curve | line with the diagonal reference | AUC printed in the corner, not only in a legend |
| Cumulative gain / lift | line, leads contacted (%) vs conversions captured (%) | **the 20% mark is annotated directly on the curve** — this is the headline number, so it is labelled on the chart, not left to the reader |
| Score distribution by outcome | two overlaid histograms (converted / not) | `#1E40AF` and `#D97706` at 0.7 opacity; direct series labels, no colour-only encoding |
| Feature importance | horizontal bar, top 10, sorted | single colour `#1E40AF`; no rainbow; value labels at the bar ends |
| Per-lead reasons | three labelled rows with an up/down marker | a word and an arrow, never colour alone |

Rules for all: no 3D, no dual axes, no pie charts, no gradient fills, axes labelled with units, data-ink first. Every figure has a one-line caption saying what it shows.

## Accessibility — checked, not assumed

- Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 everywhere; verified for every pair above.
- No information by colour alone: grades carry letters, series carry labels, directions carry arrows and words.
- Full keyboard operation; visible focus using `--color-ring`.
- Charts have a text alternative: every figure's numbers also exist in a table or caption on the model card page.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured — transitions dropped, final state rendered.
- Usable at 1024 px and at 1440 px. Phone is out of scope for an internal data tool and that is stated rather than half-attempted.

## Pre-delivery checklist

- [ ] SVG icons only — no emoji as iconography
- [ ] One call-to-action per page, in accent
- [ ] Hover transitions 150–300 ms, none longer
- [ ] Contrast 4.5:1 minimum, verified
- [ ] Focus visible on every interactive element
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion` respected
- [ ] Tables scroll inside their wrapper, never the page
- [ ] Every state above has a screen
- [ ] Numbers in tabular figures, aligned
- [ ] Model version visible on every page
